Title: Safe purchase Review: There are better kick drum mics on the market, but this one is a solid performer that has achieved near de facto status. It is equally good for recording and live performance. It's also a reasonable mic solution for capturing a double bass (i.e., stand up bass) that does not have a pickup.

It's a bit on the heavy side, so can be awkward when used with mini mic stands that a lot of drummers use. Some of those are decent, and some are flimsy, but all take up stage real estate. I use a DW DWSM2141MA Claw Hook Clamp Mic Arm, which reduces stage clutter and takes the guesswork out how to effectively mount the mic. I have included a photo to illustrate this.

You can spend a lot more and get marginally better microphones, or you can play it safe and get this one. There is a reason why you will find this mic on stages and in studios - it's a safe choice that is built to withstand the road as well as clumsy handling and still perform.

Title: Not 100% Pleased with Quality Review: I purchased mine to use as a sub mixer and to run the output through a [[ASIN:B0002CZU56 BBE 882i Sonic Maximizer]] into two channels on a [[ASIN:B001Q5S99M Peavey XR8300 8 Channel 600 watt Powered Mixer]] for larger PA configurations or into an [[ASIN:B000J2N61O American Audio Vlp300 Amplifier]] for smaller ones. See my customer-supplied image above if you are interested in how I have it configured.

I'd been told that this brand was notorious for failures and poor quality, but I was seduced by features and price and purchased it anyway. My mistake because within a month of relatively light use the fader on channel 2 started cutting out if I increased it to the top. I normally do not set it that high, so the mixer is still usable. That is not the point - the real issue is if I am already experiencing component and subsystem failures on this mixer, then what is next? I am sorry to say that I should have heeded the warnings and purchased an equivalent, such as the [[ASIN:B0002ABOFI ALESIS MultiMix 12R Audio Mixer]], which enjoys a reputation for reliability and is not that much more expensive than the Behringer RX1202FX.

Had I not experienced the failure I would have been very pleased with this mixer, and sincerely hope quality has improved since purchasing mine in November 2011. In all other respects - except quality - this is a feature rich mixer that works well ... when it works.

Title: Holds the G-Track Pro Review: Got this to use with my G-Track Pro. It IS sturdy enough to hold it in any position. After two weeks, there hasn't been any sagging or movement. It stays where I put it and only moves when I want it.

Metal is nice, but there are a few scratches on it. The joints are tight and springy, too, so it works really well with the heavier microphone attached. I'd go so far as to say this might be useful to hold a DSLR for overhead shots. The desk mount is really solid and has decent padding.

Had to give it four stars because there was some extra work to do when I got it out of the box. I had to hand tighten the joints with a Philips head screwdriver as they were each a bit loose. Also had to use a wrench to attach my microphone mount because the metal piece it attaches to kept spinning. Also...I didn't get any velcro cable ties??

Overall, though, this is a pretty great mount. After initial setup it has been working perfectly for me. Glad I trusted the reviews on this one. It really is heavy duty!

Title: great portable amp/speaker for any musical instrument with a guitar-style output cable

Review: This is a great compact lightweight 3-in-1 device, much more than your typical bluetooth speaker. The main feature is the electric guitar input, which will also work with any instrument using the same type of audio output channel. You don't need a separate amp; this device has an amplifier with basic gain/tone/level/delay controls. The speaker isn't loud or bassy enough to entertain a crowd, but it is great for practicing alone or jamming with a couple of friends. An aux input jack lets your buddy plug in a synthesizer and you can you can stream additional tracks from your smartphone via Bluetooth. This device gives you a lot of functionality in a very compact package. Just don't expect really booming sound from small 2-pound speaker. Battery life is rated at 6 hours, but obviously that depends on how loud you push it.

The Optiweb to me, nearly lives up to Elixir's claims of sounding indistinguishable from a non-coated string, but not quite. I still prefer the sound and feel of uncoated strings, especially considering the price difference.

These are a nice option for the corrosion-resistance though, if that's a particular issue for you.

Title: A Nice Solution at a Nice Price

Review: Had assorted ukuleles, a guitar, and a banjo that needed off-the-floor homes. These hangers hold all the instruments with ease - smallest ukulele, thin neck of the banjo, regular sized guitar etc. I did opt to use slightly longer screws than those provided just because I always do - but I think the included screws will be fine for most uses. Happy to have our house less cluttered feeling, our instruments more safely stored, and a nice-looking new wall display to boot.

Title: Disappointed This

Review: I have ordered this bag twice and both times they did not fit my 10 inch conga drum. I am very disappointed, I have other bags from this company and I don't know why this bag has not fit.

Title: Decent option for the price, but I wouldn't trust my high end product in it

Review: They are a decent option for the price. However, be aware that they are not super high quality. The bottom portion of the stand only slides in and has lots of room to rotate around. So you need to make to place the instrument in the device, strap in the neck and ensure that it is sitting straight before walking away or else it can tip and slide out. I like how adjustable it is since we have a number of different sized guitars that needed a place to go. But if I wanted a stand for one of the more expensive instruments, I would choose a different option than these.

Title: Good value

Review: I repair and refinish electric guitars and occasionally find that I need to replace a pickup. I ordered these and a couple of other sets (different colors) so I would have some on hand for quick installs. I have used these to replace a failed or flaky pickup and they seem to work quite well. Sure, there are much hotter pickups available, but the price comes with it. For an inexpensive pickup that works adequately, these have seemed to work well. In that sense I consider them good value for the price.

Title: Effective and beautiful Review: I had an old cable that kept crackling and had loose contacts...

No more! The added benefit of the right angle adapter is a nice touch.

This moves easily and flexes well for stage play. I appreciate the quality construction and the sound is top notch.

No regrets

Title: I got the ugly duckling box & the "I don't care how we packaged this to ship" banjo

Review: I have no idea how the product actually is.  It's a gift for my son for Christmas.  I just hope it wasn't damaged...it was not UPS's fault in my opinion as the product wasn't wrapped in any fashion just taped shut with brown packing tape.  I work in a warehouse and I know that it could have been prepared for shipping better than that.  Thank God it was UPS that delivered it and not Fedex.  I recommend you purchase musical instruments from inside a store and not online.

Title: Great bag if it was more durable

Review: The bag is really great for the price except for one thing: the straps are not very durable. I’ve had for a month and one of the shoulder straps have already ripped to the point of not being able to use it. Would give it 5 stars if it wasn’t for this.

Title: Not what I thought

Review: I received the condenser shown but no clip, no mic ....just the condenser ..I feel ripped off

Title: Setup & installation is so convoluted I sent back!

Review: Setup process is not at all user friendly

Title: Good Choice Review: Pros: excellent sound reproduction; comfortable; fits a wide variety of head sizes; masks outside sounds
Cons: fits so closely tends to be hot after lengthy wear;

Title: User Friendly Keyboard

Review: I purchased a cheap, no name brand keyboard for my teenager a year ago. It was not a good quality keyboard at all. She disliked it so much, she rarely played it. I got her a nice Yamaha one which was much better. It was also a higher price. My son wanted to play around with a keyboard to create MIDI sounds for his video games and my teens weren't thrilled about sharing a keyboard, so I got him this Casio instrument.  I would say that this Casio one is a nice middle ground keyboard. It's better than the cheap no name one It's completely adequate for a beginning teenager (or child) who wants to learn or play around with a keyboard. He did have to purchase a specialized cable to hook it up to his laptop, but that was expected. The keys sound a little plastic sounding, but not as bad as the first keyboard I got. The plastic sounds are pretty standard for portable keyboards in my opinion.  This keyboard has been fairly user friendly. It was easy to set up. For the price, it does a good job. When my son played with the cheap one, he expressed his desire for a better keyboard. With this one, he's satisfied with it's performance for his needs.

Title: Just a bit tight for my son's Yamaha horn.

Review: We bought one of these for my son's Yamaha trumpet, for starting high school marching band. The YAC-1500G was not a drop in replacement, it required filing down to get the lyre post to fit into the pinky ring. Works fine after being 'customized' to suit. Just sort of surprised that this - the only Yamaha lyre I found - wouldn't fit a common student model horn.

Title: Spikes are perfect - size, shape, material and gauge - Shred, Pinch, Articulate Review: I don't have to "spike" my picks anymore! Since about 1985, I would buy my Tortex picks (usually greens .88mm, sometimes yellows .73mm). I would borrow my girlfriend's nail files, until she/they finally bought me a few of my own.
I'd just carefully file a point, nearly identical to that of the "Spike" - but, I wasn't always as consistent. These are .80mm - RIGHT IN BETWEEN TORTEX YELLOW AND GREEN --- I felt like Goldilocks' ... manly brother ;-) because this gauge is just right. The point allows for an attack that cannot be had with a traditional pick's more rounded tip. A friend of mine was doing it as I recall - he was recording with Randy Jackson, among others (a great player). I have occasionally tried other picks - picks like Dava picks which have various styles to aid in GRIP. I file them to a point of course. But, I keep coming back to the Clayton Spike Ultem Gold Sharp Standard. It just _feels_ right for me. I play better.

Title: only accurate to 10 cents Review: This is a small lightweight inexpensive tuner. Smaller than any of the other battery-operated tuners that I own. The screen responds very quickly when I pluck a string on my instrument. The screen displays white when you are out-of-tune and green when you are in-tune. I use the chromatic mode with all my instruments; I don't see the point of the other modes.

The screen is not as detailed as most other tuners. The display is accurate to 10.0 cents, which may be OK for recreational musicians. Some other tuners in this price range are accurate to 1.0 cents, which is much more precise and that is desirable if you want to be in tune with other people in a band. For more money, you can buy tuners that are accurate to 0.1 cents, which is good for studio work.

The body of the tuner is all lightweight plastic. I don't know how sturdy it will be; hopefully at least as sturdy as those Snark tuners that tend to break at the neck.

Title: It's pretty neat the way they can print these

Review: It's pretty neat the way they can print these, and overall it looks very good.  If you really want to scrutinize it, the color calibration might be a little bit off between the orange and red, and there are a few tiny smudges or errant speckles of color, but no-one's going to notice on a product like this in use.  The leather ends are decent, no problem, but I'd prefer if they were a little shorter and also I like straps where the one end is sewn on directly.  The rings that attach the ends are plastic, while the adjuster thing seems to be metal painted black, but it all feels durable enough.  I got Rainbow Dash, Fluttershy, and Muffins.

Review: It doesn't work very well.

Title: They are ok; temp fix until I can get speaker stands.

Review: It did remove *some* feedback when playing a record on my turntable, which sits on the same table as the speaker, but I can still feel vibrations on the table even with these under the speaker - which sometimes causes the audio to suffer. I'll probably still upgrade to speaker stands to get them off the table, however.

Title: Great size for my Air 49.

Review: Great size for my Air 49. Very solid at chair hight. If you need to stand and play though, go with a larger stand.

Title: Terrible range - sounds cheap

Review: Saw someone using this with moderate results. Mine didn't fare so well. Tried every conceivable modification, location, and setup. Same tinny/short range distorted sound most cheap mics have. Less than 10-15 feet, it works OK. But then what's the point of going wireless?

Title: First compressor ever. Review: I have been buying and using guitar pedals for almost 50 years - probably close to 200 of them - but never a compressor. Didn't see the need for one.
Then I came across this Amazon Basics pedal at a very attractive price, and thought "Why not"?
Tell you what. It's solid. It's quiet. It squishes. It sustains. It does much of what vastly more expensive pedals do.
It doesn't necessarily play nicely with some of my other pedals, though. Although I'm still learning it, my overdrives and distortions don't like the compression in front of them.

Title: Great product for electronic drums and practice pads with rims

Review: I put these on three of my Pintech 10" pads and the 12" one I used for a snare.  Made rimshots and cross sticking acoustically quieter in the room and when doing lots of them, didn't damage the sticks like a metal rim does over time.  I did find them a bit slow and fidgety to press onto each pad's rim, but once they were on, they worked perfectly.  4 1/2 stars.

Review: Very nice sound in super small size, please don't lose you wind puff.  Without it this mic is a lil too good.

Review: Everything was pretty good, nothing wrong with the product except that the metal keys looked kind of dirty? Almost like someone smudged them or something. No harm done, just ruined the "pristine"-ness of the unpacking. Normally I wouldn't be bothered at all by it but given the pandemic going on it made me question it a little.

Review: Fairly light. Nice cushioned handle. Good extension length. Integrated cable is nice. Unfortunately, the twisting lock mechanism is poorly engineered and could use some improvements. Overall for the price this was a decent buy. I just wish the twist mechanism was a bit more robust.

Title: The sound of the lower range notes is quite nice, the sound of the upper range notes seem ...

Review: I purchased one of these for my grandson for Christmas.  It arrived without any problems in a timely manner.  The sound of the lower range notes is quite nice, the sound of the upper range notes seem a little out of tune (flat). The price was good, although the mallets that came with it looked as though they were used.  They were very scarred around the largest part of the ball which would strike the keys.  The keyboard itself did not look used but the mallets looked as though they were some possibly returned from another customer.  If I had to do over again, I would probably have spent the extra money and got one with a stand.  The CB percussion set may sound better although it has less amount of notes. Title: Good product

Review: This is a great product. I have not played my violin in a couple years and needed some reminders where to place my fingers. It was easy to apply and is mostly clear so it does not show on my violin. I do wish the colored lines were a bit darker or brighter, some of them are hard to see looking down the neck.

Review: Would give better rating if the software that came with it worked. The website says it's down every time you try to download the software. Is there a fix to this?

Been using it for a long time and haven't found a need to upgrade.
The only thing I've changed is I took off the three legs and invested in a desktop microphone stand just to get it closer to my face.
Other than that If you're looking for an affordable/reliable microphone I'd highly recommend this.

Review: It works as well or better than the cheap headset attached microphones and the lighting is fairly nice. Headphone pass-through is also a convenient future. Overall, pleasantly surprised with this purchase. Not the best audio quality but the other features balance out.

Review: It was easy for me to hook up these mics to our current set-up. However, I've noticed that these mic produce a bit of static and the sound quality isn't clear.

Review: This is really a lot of fun.  I used it extensively for pad and soundscapes on a film score project.  I only wish I had bought the fancier one because it would be fun to try it with my friend's Moog! Feels well-made.  Great sounds with the Lié software

Title: This is so much fun! A small quality control problem with the stand

Review: This is an amazing keyboard with a nice (default) piano sound. It has many options for both beginners and more advanced players. It has built-in speakers with adjustable volume and also a pair of headphones (so others in the house or in the next apartment won't have to listen to you practice.) There is an option for recording what you play, and even a microphone. The included stool is padded and very comfortable. There's also a nice stand which doesn't even require a screwdriver to assemble (the only required assembly.) It all went together perfectly except for the last screw (both screws have nice handles.) That last one would not go into the bottom of the keyboard at all. This was a little discouraging because everything else about this product was so beautiful. Actually, one screw would probably have been enough to hold the keyboard to the stand. The keyboard unit is flat and sits firmly on the stand. My husband and I did finally decide to put a loop of duct tape where the second screw would have fit. It's fine and I even feel sheepish about taking off a star, but if this had been a gift, some people might have been put off. This is a delightful instrument. It's good for beginners, yet has lots of features to grow into. Love it!

Title: dull bass

Review: I just switched to these from Hannabach Silver Special.  I use them on a Spanish import classical guitar with a cedar top. The trebles are fine, but the wound bass strings have no depth.  It's like they're lacking the fundamental and just have a lot of overtones.  The sound has no presence.  I thought the Hannabach (which I used for about 12 years) were a little cold sounding when I first put them on but otherwise a brilliant sound.  They'd be ideal for concert sound.  Then I had switched from the warmest strings I've used with the best depth: Rotosound Superia.  I know that's not a name normally affiliated with classical guitar, but they sounded great to my ears.  Now I wonder if I should try Savarez Corum or go away to another brand.

Title: Rusted bad weld on Z-arm. Arm fell off at weld.

Review: The lower tier left Z-arm had a bad rusted weld at the hinge, and the arm fell off when I was assembling it. Mine was sold by Amazon. The carton was somewhat beat up. I ordered a replacement from Adorama, and will update this review when that arrives and I run it through its paces.

Title: Both cables crapped out after 2 years

Review: Going by the positive reviews I bought these cables back in 2020. One of them I had to replace within a few months and now both are completely worthless. I was also hearing a hum from my amplifier thinking there was something wrong with it. Turned out to be the cables.

Title: Gave this to my son as he is the electric guitar player

Review: Well, I do play guitar, but it is a lap steel guitar, so this gadget really would not work well for my style of guitar.  Anyway, my son reached out and bought himself a high-dollar guitar that he loves to play and I have given him a few smaller items to try with that guitar like a stomp box that he likes, but thought this might be a way to try something a little different.  Now, I am the one with a headphone "thing" - I have at least five over-the-ear headphones that are near top-of-the-line type, a couple of them have such good sound it's amazing. I mention this because I gave my son three of my OTE headphones to try and pick the best that would work with this effects plug in.  He did note that one of the headphones seem to have more noise than the others, but I did tell him to try with and without the noise cancellation that each set has a button for.  My $450 set which was the medium priced of the three pairs apparently held the best sound for him and I gave him that pair to use (for now - they are still my headphones!).  As far as the effects go, he told me they aren't all exactly as they are noted to be, but each one added a bit of uniqueness to his practice sessions.  He said he wouldn't use it when he was jamming with his friends, but that when he's home and wants to just fool around with sound while practicing, this little unit would be good for that.

Title: Nice tone. Pretty singing bowl.

Review: This small, metal singing bowl has decoration worked into the metal. It comes with a mallet and a pillow to set the bowl on, though you can also strike the bowl while you are holding it. It makes a lovely sound when you strike it, but I'm still working on being able to consistently make it "sing" by running the mallet around the outside of the rim. They do not really include directions on how to use it, only on the historical use of a Tibetan singing bowl. They state that singing bowls are made out of seven metals: gold, silver, mercury, copper, iron, tin, lead. Considering those metals, I was surprised that a suggested use was to cook food in them. They state that there are five basic techniques for playing the bowls, but they do not describe these techniques beyond: beating, encircling, adding of water, adding of toneless bowls, and spinning.

Title: It worked great! Until it didn't anymore 25 days old. :( Review: I read other one star reviews suspiciously. There were plenty of happy 4 or 5 star reviews too so I ordered it. I loved this little speaker. I used it a couple times a week for an hour or so each time. Then just shy of the one month mark, it suddenly started acting up just like the 1 star reviews mentioned.

I changed the battery to a new one. It would play fine for a minute but then start cutting out, with no sound. The "on indicator" light would pulsate from bright to dim, slowly to bright again. Paranoid about the battery still, I tried yet another brand new Duracell 9 volt. Same thing.

I was just 2 days shy of the 30 day Amazon return period and just sent it back today for a refund. I am disappointed because when it did work, I really liked it. I am going to go order another (more expensive) model now.

Amazon's return system is fantastic. As soon as they received notification of the item coming back, they issued the refund. They even paid for it to be shipped back. That is the only silver lining in this story. It is obvious they have a quality control issue. I know you get what you paid for but in this case I didn't even get that much.

Title: Feels cheap

Review: If you've ever used another clip-on tuner you'll find this one almost unusable. I wish my old blue Snark tuner had kept working properly. The SN5X is slow to react to a note, making tuning a frustrating experience. It's not as precise, with fewer gradations. The plastic and build quality are definitely cheaper. And the clip isn't nearly as strong.

Review: Did not work and bought two of them..  Not happy.

Title: Looks great, works great! Review: The wood grain finish seems like a durable enamel coating and looks very good. It's obvious when handling it that it's made of a sturdy metal material, but the faux wood finish does a decent job of not standing out too much on a wooden stringed instrument if you're trying to preserve a more natural look. The capo has a fairly powerful spring and does a great job of holding down all the strings on the bar. It has a black rubber interior surface to protect the neck of your instrument on both sides. There is another bit of black rubber padding on the thumb grip as well.

The two "wood grain" picks that came with it don't look even remotely like real wood, but they're just little extras and I didn't make this purchase for them so I'm leaving them out of my rating score entirely. If you want real or convincing faux wooden picks I would suggest getting them somewhere else.

Title: I have a couple of tremolo harmonicas from the 1960s and they are wonderfully tuned. I suspect its the chords on the ...

Review: The tuning of this harmonica is not what I expected.  I have a couple of tremolo harmonicas from the 1960s and they are wonderfully tuned.  I suspect its the chords on the lower end of this one.  Some people find this tuning to their liking, but I cannot get used to it.

Title: These are good headphones. I use them for listening to music ...

Review: These are good headphones. I use them for listening to music and so on through my laptop and I rate the performance as quite good. However, I am not an audiophile and in any case have a noticeable high frequency hearing loss so my rating is not going to be very useful. I was looking for an unpowered, non-bluetooth headphone for day-to-day use, and this one fills the bill in every way except one: the cord is permanently attached to the headphone. In fact, the cord is slightly too long for my needs and as a result tends to get tangled up in things, including the rolling wheel of my chair. If the cord plugged into the headphone, then I could get a shorter one, and if the existing one were to be damaged (e.g., by the rolling wheel of my chair), then I could easily replace it. If the cord were a plug-in, I would have given the product five stars.

Review: Desk issue isn't company fault, its mine. However the sturdiness is another topic. It doesn't hold very well. Maybe with a light mic it can, with my KSM model Shure, not so well.

When do you really need it? When you are performing and it is vital that it works accurately. This tool is prone to puzzling misreadings of notes, and sometimes (usually when you're in a hurry to get to the next number, or a new tuning) it doesn't show anything at all. I'm going to splash out on an LRBaggs Venue, then I'll be able to tune and have all the other functions. I simply don't understand how this model can get so many stars; I've tried placing it differently, and playing loud and soft: nothing works consistently. The best strategy on the low 'E' is to play the harmonic, but even then, the needle zooms to somewhere near the center, depending on the tuning, then immediately flashes backwards to 'off.' Don't waste your money.
I have been an acoustic guitarist for many years.

Title: Good price but... But I can only give it 3 stars because of that problem. Check out the before and after pics I uploaded, the new tremolo looks awesome, I still can't believe it fitted so well! It saved me a lot of plugging and drilling that I thought I was going to have to do on my old Charvel.
Update Feb 27, 2021
I bought an original Floyd Rose bar and all I had to do was countersink the instalation hole in the tremolo and voila! See new added pic, I paid 14.00 for the Floyd bar here at Amazon, and now it's fully functional.

Excellent for me and others with musical instruments that are difficult to "electrify."

Title: Good budget-friendly multipurpose cardioid condenser mic Review: Well known in the recording industry, Tascam delivers a multi-purpose home recording cardioid condenser for the budget-minded.

Utilizing an 18mm diaphragm, larger than the majority of the Tascam microphone line, frequency response is stated being very wide at 20hz-20khz. This combined with the circuit design produces an equalization profile relatively even up to mids around 1khz, with boosts starting at 6.5khz to 10khz, rolling off noticeably upward. Lack of a pad is somewhat made up for
by a stated SPL of 136dB, which adds to the options one can record.

Sources such as cymbals came through well with upper register accents, and string instruments produce a defined body. Mid and high response can compliment higher range voices, although a low cut switch would be a great addition to clean up excess low end frequencies. The aluminium body construction is solid, but out-of-studio use would not be recommended. Overall the microphone makes a good complement to other mics due to the upper mid/high emphasis.

Considering that accessories include a shock mount, mini desk stand, and short XLR cable, the TM-80 would make a great addition to a home studio looking for versatility with affordability.

Pros: Great mid and high response. Full body from the low mids. Solid build quality.

Cons: Lack of Pad/Low Cut switch. Mid vocal frequency lacks emphasis. Rolloff above 10k can lead to “radio” sound

Title: I love Tascam, but tragically flawed with poor shielding - would have been the best in class

Review: Huge fan of Tascam, but the DR-05X has a tragic flaw, and that is poor shielding. In a controlled environment with little to no RF traffic, this is a better recorder than its primary competitor, the Zoom H1n (which I also own). However, RF interference is everywhere these days, especially in crowded or city environments, and this is a tremendous disappointment about how they handled the design of the shielding for this otherwise excellent product. Now this is primarily with the built-in mics, so if you exclusively use a lav, for example, you may have much better luck. But if you ever use the built-in mics in an area with strong RF signals present (which is more common than I thought it would be), watch out, your recordings could be ruined by the interference. It's not just cell phones that cause problems up close, it's any other kind of radio or wireless signal, which is everywhere in a city. I've been doing testing and it's amazing how much interference this picks up in some areas. Just very very unfortunate since Tascam usually makes incredible equipment. So if you have to use built-in mics, I'd strongly suggest the H1n, which has far better shielding. Hoping that Tascam fixes this problem so I can get back on board the Tascam team with the next release of their recorders.

I put a set of these on a Gibson SG Standard and the Gibson screws had a head that was too large in diameter. I then placed the stock screw in a drill, just like you would place a drill bit, and ran it accross a file until the diameter of the stock screw head was small enough to fit the Dunlop strap button.

Title: Not As Advertised--Plays And Sounds Okay Review: I went looking for a beginner dulcimer to see if I was interested in playing the instrument. This dulcimer from Roosebeck looked to be a good choice. The instrument is made in Pakistan, and is a decent sounding dulcimer. You can adjust the space between the strings to suit your style of playing and that's a good thing. I recommend this instrument as a first, beginner dulcimer. When/if you get good at it, you'll absolutely want something much better.

My issues with the instrument I received are that it DOES NOT MATCH the product description/pictures:
1) It does not have the features as shown in the listing.
2) The nut and bridge were not glued down and, consequently, fall off when restringing or adjusting string distances. It is generally accepted practice to put down a little glue to hold the nut and bridge in place. No, it doesn't need to be epoxied onto the wood. It does, and should, however, be attached to the neck by something other than string pressure.
3) The strings are cheap, cheap, cheap. If you're going to buy one of these, do include a set of strings and do a change out as soon as you receive the instrument.

I only recommend this dulcimer if it's your first instrument, or you're buying it for a student.

Title: Tiny Amp, Big On Features Review: his is a tiny amp that is just right for practice in environments where there is not a lot of background noise. It's more than adequate if you are practicing in a quiet room though.

The main selling point of this amp is not the quantity of audio output but the quality in regards to the effects, distortion, tone and other mods you can manually make to the sound. It has n incredible array of built-in options for such a low priced practice amp.

In addition to being able to straight plug into your guitar the amp also offers Bluetooth input as well, which is another huge extra for a product in it's price range. If you're not a really small person, this is an excellent choice for an acoustic dreadnaught style guitar.

Title: I like Aquila strings, but my girlfriend doesn't Review: Realistically, there is no best ukulele string for everyone. I love these strings on my laminate mid-range ukulele. The girlfriend thinks they are too harsh for her solid-acacia ukulele and she replaced her strings with flouro-carbons. If you read the ukulele nerd forums, you will see long discussions about ukulele strings and different people disagreeing about which strings are best even for the same brand and model of instrument. Bottom line is the best strings for you are a personal decision, based largely on what sound you like and what kind of music you play and what is your skill level. Strings are cheap enough and easy enough to install that, as soon as you develop a good enough ear to tell the difference, you may as well try a few on your ukulele and figure it out for yourself.

As with all ukulele strings, they do take a while to settle in. I had to tune them after every 15 minutes of playing for the first couple of days. Every 30 minutes for the next few days. Once an hour for the next week. After a month, I only have to tune them a couple of times a week (or when the room is much cooler or warmer).

Title: I wanted to love this but ... Review: Having purchased a batch of these (nearly a dozen) I thought I had hit the mother lode of great deals. However, they began to fail at an alarming rate, rendering them unusable for live performances.

The cause of the failures appears to be the solders at the connectors. It is a relatively easy fix if you are handy with a soldering gun, but also frustrating when you expect cables to work out of the box and provide a reasonable service life.

As others have noted these do not appear to be true 12n gauge cables - perhaps 14 gauge is a closer call. I have no problem with that aspect because despite what looks like poor manufacturing and assembly at the connectors the cables seem to be high quality and when they do work they are relatively noise free. Those characteristics earned this cable three stars in my opinion instead of a lower rating.

Title: teak is just colored plastic, beat ringer doesn't work, lasts about 15 minutes at 100bpm Review: There are lots of free metronome apps for smartphones or even your web browser. This mechanical metronome has a nice retro look and feel, but also a lot of problems. The windup mechanism only lasts about 15 minutes (at 100bpm), which is fine for practicing songs that are shorter than that. You set the beats per minute with an analog slider and it does seem accurate enough for practice use in the first half of my 15 minutes, but it does noticeably fade after that. There is a slider that is supposed to ring a bell every 2, 3, 4, or 6 beats, but mine never worked reliably.

We got the "teak" model thinking it was made of real wood since it costs twice as much as the other models. No, it is just colored plastic like the cheaper models. Don't waste your money.

The unit comes with no instructions, so if it isn't working for you, there is no way to tell if you are using it wrong or if it is broken.

Title: I use them as stereo speakers in my living room and they have been great. Symphonic orchestra sound is very clear and accurate Review: I own a pair for about three years now, I use them as stereo speakers in my living room and they have been great. Symphonic orchestra sound is very clear and accurate, which was my primary goal.
I would also like to note that accuracy remains even at low volume, so it's possible to listen to music and then have a conversation without having to adjust the volume. With normal speakers I had a problem - to get full detail I had to crank up the volume, but then I can't talk to anyone. Studio monitors solved this problem quite well for me.

I had some amount of 60hz buzzing, that went away after my last move, so it was likely related to the electric wiring. I'm using coax cables and connectors, so that's probably why. It was impossible to get an hdmi receiver with balanced inputs, which is the recommended setup, instead of coax.

All in all I am very happy with these.

Title: More expensive and didn't work as well as SNARK Review: Could not figure out a way to clip it to my electric Skyinbow violin. Won't clip to pegs, won't clip to body, so couldn't really use. When I did get it to clip a few times (before it slipped off), I would play the note (with it set to violin) but nothing would register. Then when I stopped playing the note, suddenly the "A" or whichever string I had just played would light up, and it always showed a range--never a solid note (and yes, I was in tune). My ear works better than this tuner. A bandmate gave me a Snark, and it works MUCH better and stays clipped to the peg while I am tuning. When I tune, I tune the A, then do the other strings by ear, unless it is REALLY noisy. I double check everything with the tuner, and I am always spot on (and find this to be the case no matter which tuner I use, even an old school tuning fork). So the fact that this Intelli Tuner did not work for me indicates that it is no good. The reviews were good, so I was disappointed that it was a bad purchase.

Go with the inexpensive SNARK. It comes in a little bag you can tuck into your case, it seems to pick up minor tuning differences better, the head adjusts more easily and in more positions. The Intelli Tuner just didn't work as well.

Title: Superior quality stand and the only real choice for some uses Review: Construction is superior to the plethora of no-name or off-name brand stands that flood the market. More importantly, it's simple to assemble and musician-friendly when it comes to folding and transporting it.

The base is also solid and steady. I had some initial concerns because I had been using tripod style stands, but those concerns have been assuaged by perfect steadiness of this stand, even when loaded with a full stick bag I mentioned above.

Not only is this stand a godsend, but it has sold me on the fact that purchasing a Manhasset is an investment in gear that will last. No more off-brand stands for me.

Title: Not what I was expecting Review: Yamaha keyboards are all great for certain things and I was hoping this unit was an upgrade for the one I've had since 2004. Only to find out my 2004 version has better configuration and memory features. I was hoping to be able to download songs and import them into the keyboard. It says you can, but you need to be a MIDI wizard to understand the process. Bottom line is, after hours of searching I have not found a single word of actual instructions. You need to be a sound engineer to even understand the formatting.
There is no memory on this keyboard, no place to insert a thumb drive which is what it says to use on Yamaha's music website. So you need to connect to a computer and the keyboard at the same time. And you are on you own as far as actually getting the song from the computer to the keyboard. I gave up on downloading.
Another drawback for me is no configuration features on the auto-accompaniments. It is what it is. My old unit allowed you to change everything or omit parts, You could ad in brass or strings or different voices. Make up your own versions.
My last disappointment is you can't store a configuration (no memory) so after you spend 45 minutes selecting everything for a song and fine-tuning tempo and whatever, as soon as you power off, it's all gone. My old unit would allow me to save a configuration.
Bottom Line.....If I had know it was this limited, I would have not purchased it.

Title: Almost perfect - the headsets are the weak link Review: I purchased this as a home rehearsal system, as well as a back-up for the Audio-Technica system I use for gigs. Since there are a number of detailed reviews already I will keep mine short and to the point.

First, the weak part is the headsets. They are uncomfortable and if you wear glasses they are also not optimal, nor are they easy to adjust. However, I have to give the microphones in them a lot of credit because they do sound good. I did not try the lavalier mics and do not intend to since I do not use those. I do wish the headset from my Audio-Technica system would fit the body packs that come with this one because I would purchase two of those to replace the ones that came with this kit.

The receiver is truly nice. It's fairly easy to set up and configure despite the poor instructions, and the ability to run it off batteries is a plus for some folks. I do not foresee me using batteries, but I know musicians who have battery operated amps and PAs who would love that particular feature.

Sound quality is very good bordering on outstanding, and the overall value is darn good for what you get. If this came with the same quality headsets as those with my Audio-Technica I would give this a solid five stars. If I had to doit all over I would have invested in a second Audio-Technica set, but that is my personal opinion. I cannot fault the sound quality, and if you need to play where there is no electricity, this is hard to beat.

Title: These are not silent like dog whistles, if you were wondering Review: I got this set of two whistles for me and my partner to wear around our necks in the house to blow when the dogs bark "inappropriately." I don't know what it is about UPS trucks...maybe they look like big bears or something...but our three little dogs go absolutely nuts when UPS comes, far more so than when FedEx or Amazon trucks show up. I have never heard such caterwauling. Squirt guns help, but we never seem to have them nearby when needed or else they are empty.

The dog whistles we've tried in the past don't really work that well; we can't hear them and do wonder if they make any sound at all that the dogs can hear. These whistles make a high-pitched sound that we can hear, and they do have an effect on the dogs...especially when both of us blow on them at the same time! The whistles are not very loud unless you blow hard on them, though, but I do like that you can control the level of sound with your breath. I love that they are brass and look pretty indestructible. The lanyards are a good length for wearing, and the clip on the end is easy to open but strong. We had to tighten up the brass ring on one whistle with pliers. I like that I have mine accessible whether I'm inside the house or outside in the garden.

Title: You get what you pay for Review: This was one of the cheapest ukuleles on Amazon at the time of my purchase. It was intended as a gift to a young child as a beginner instruments but I ended up having to purchase a different instrument as this one was not giftable IMHO.

This ukulele has so many problems I don't know where to begin. The finish quality is horrible. There are rough patches and even areas where the stain and finish are completely missing. The action is very poor. Nut is high, so it would be difficult for a beginner to play even simple chords in the first position. Intonation is poor to begin with, I don't think the frets have been placed exactly where they need to be. The extremely high saddle makes the intonation even worse. By the time you get to the 12th fret, it's off by almost a quarter tone. Basically, any chord that includes an open string sounds out of tune. The factory strings are also very poor quality, and keep stretching and falling out of tune over a just a few minutes. This may be normal when you first tune a ukulele with new strings, but the same behavior after several days of use is unacceptable.

Basically, if you are looking for a cheap toy for a young child for pretend play, it may be a good deal, but as a musical instrument, it is worthless.

Title: Well worth the money

Review: I have a new Franz Hoffmann Etude Viola that I purchased from Shar music. It has ebony pegs and fingerboard. The pegs were very difficult to turn and some felt like they were going to break with the force required to move them. This made it impossible to tune each string. I purchased this peg compound and completely removed my A string peg (I would watch one of the videos on YouTube to learn how to do this correctly. DO NOT remove all strings at the same time!). I removed my A peg, coated it with this compound which has the thickness and consistency of semi-soft red clay. I then inserted the peg, turned it around a few times, removed it again and gave it another coat. With the string off I also used a little on the Nut and Bridge where the string touched. I then rewound the string and moved on to my D string. After coating all the pegs in this way I was then able to easily, and smoothly, tune each string and come very close to a perfect note by just tuning with the pegs and not the fine tuners. I've noticed no slippage either. This was well worth the money in my case and I highly recommend this product !

Title: It sucks tone less and is way more accurate to the ...

Review: I directly compared this with a few other spring reverb pedals. This pedals normal signal is worlds above the Boss FRV-1 and most other spring reverb pedals. It sucks tone less and is way more accurate to the sounds of a spring reverb outboard unit. It can even do the semi-distorted tones of '60s Spy music like the old James Bond theme. However, it had a personal deal-breaker: it lacked the watery drip of a reverb unit. When I palm-muted it sounded very digital, almost like a modulation effect was on it (I know about the Easter Egg, this is not it.) Listen to the intro of Esperanza by Dick Dale and you'll know what I mean. To most people this will not matter, but it's a deal-breaker for spring reverb for me. Good pedal otherwise.

Title: Doesn't work with actual sound boards

Review: I was looking for a wireless lavalier mic that could be used primarily with a sound board but also a smart phone or laptop. I thought it had the right plug for the sound board, but the mic only worked for about 1 second when everything was plugged in and turned on. It's easy to charge the battery on both the mic and the receiver (and I'd done so before trying them out). I'll update when I get a chance to try it out plugged into a phone for vlogging, but I wanted to warn people that this really is intending for computers (PC) and phones.

Title: Timely, all parts working..but..good luck tuning Review: I purchased this guitar as a Christmas gift for my son who is 8. The product came well packed and I was impressed with all facets with the exception of the guitar itself which has a problem staying in tune. You are lucky to play for more than 10 minutes without 3 of the strings going out of tune substantially. I have tried myself and familiar enough with playing to know I am not plucking too hard. If I could solve this, I would definitely give this a 4.

I did plan to notify the company. But, have had no time with travel for work.

Title: Not for Me

Review: I've been playing an Electric Bass for over 2 decades. From a 4 string fretless to 4&5 strings fretted. I wanted to try my hands on an acoustic Bass and I was disappointed. The sound for me is just god awful. I pretty much had to re-train myself how I play it because it's much wider and it feels like a big box on my body. The electric side of it works well but it's just a louder version of "god awful". If you're drinking by the camp fire you could have some fun but that's about it.

Title: I absolutely hate this mic stand

Review: I absolutely hate this mic stand. The "tightening" screws are there pretty much just for show. One little nudge and the whole thing collapses and you have to readjust. There isn't a tightening screw where the mic head is so it just keeps flopping down from the weight of the mic.

Title: Great for ring finger big for pinky

Review: It's the most solid glass slide I've ever had. It's comfortable if I'm using the ring finger. It's too loose. I wish they had inserts that fit the preferred finger.. I happen to be a dual finger player.

Title: I really wanted to love this... Review: Couldn't get this to work for me. I have a soft rubber mute that slips over my bridge, fits exactly, and nicely mutes the sound without changing it.

This mute just barely rests on bridge, mutes the sound somewhat (not as good as my rubber mute), but what's bothersome is that this mute changes the tone of my violin. It changes it to the point where every single note sounds wrong.

Back to my rubber mute! Maybe someday I'll try taking a screwdriver to this one and futzing with it, but until then, it's going in a drawer.

Title: Defective/Cheap mount!  Also be sure to read the Instructions about Nitrocellulose and Gibson finishes!

Review: As some others have said on here - Mount is cheap!  The 3 tabs that hold this to the mount, one of them was bent way out and snapped off. I never even had a chance to mount it.  Further if you have a high-end Gibson then according to the directions this isn't recommended for use with Nitrocellulose finishes it may otherwise dent your headstock!  Just thought I would mention that. Why is this not listed in the description?

Title: A standard, but good bag. Review: Well made. It does the job. I like the multiple pockets and multiple carrying handles.

Detracting 1 star because of no pockets big enough for magazine-sized books or music. You have to store it under your resonator. I don't mind that much, though.

Title: Exactly as described

Review: Comfortable thick pics, exactly as described. My only complaint is there seems to be an awful lot of noise when the pick contacts the string, which is weird because I've never seen or heard of that before. It's like a plastic clicking. I don't know if I would get them again. I think I would get the Golden Gate ones instead.

Title: Wouldn't recommend.

Review: The case is okay but the texture in the back makes it suuuuuper slippery. Wouldn't recommend.

Title: Ridiculously over-priced. My own fault for impulse buying. Review: Just read this review: http://www.amazon.com/review/R3P7MXP1P1W6LP/ref=cm_cr_dp_title?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B00EO4A7L0&channel=detail-glance&nodeID=11091801&store=musical-instruments

Title: These are NOT what I ordered and NOT what is on the box, in the directions, or on Amazon.

Review: These (two) remote key fobs are NOT what I ordered. What I got is a pair of 4 button remotes, each with a loose soft plastic panel and roman numerals on each "button." While this style may work--or may not--neither of the two I ordered has the stay, away, unlock, or panic buttons and neither has a hard plastic faceplate for the buttons to stick through. I don't care to give either to someone else and hope they could remember which numeral stood for what, even if they could be set up by the tech. The belt clip is cheap and flimsy. These will be returned as soon as possible. I was looking for additional Fobs for my ADT system and the tech said this was the brand to get. This may be the brand, but sure not the model. Interestingly, the directions, boxes, and Amazon listings are for what I wanted.  I just didn't get them.

Title: Sounded great for a few days Review: I love how these sound fresh out of the pack, but they died harder and faster than any bass strings I've played. Broke them in in a day, black spots in a week, and completely dead in a month.

If you're changing strings after every gig and need something super cheap I think these are a good option. If you expect your strings to last, go with anything else.

Title: Another don’t throw good money after bad

Review: Not nearly heavy enough to hold an 88 key keyboard. Wouldn’t recommend for kids because of the light weight giving a propensity to tip when playing.

Title: cheap way to connect an electric guitar to a PC, plug-and-play with audacity

Review: If you're looking for a cheap way to connect your guitar to your PC, give this a try. It doesn't compare well to more expensive cables in terms of durability or latency, but for basic use, it is fine. It installed plug-and-play on my PC. I am using the free Audacity audio software on my PC.

Title: Great gift for your favorite guitar player.

Review: Bought this for my husband for Father’s Day , I couldn’t wait to give it to him. He thought it was so cool. The only negative is only having one thickness of sheets to punch. He likes a thinner pick.

Title: Not sturdy at all Review: To say I am disappointed is an understatement. For my application it really gets 1-Star

The range of motion is as advertised. So no faulting there.

Sturdiness also impacts stability. This configuration is not sturdy enough for a Yeti Microphone. The issue is the mounting clamp, it is very poorly designed. This might be acceptable for a smaller microphone like the nano; however not the Yeti. The clamp is too small, the threads of the "bolt" turn through the piece that should provide more surface area on the bottom.

I don't know what to do at this point...

Title: For use as a costume accessory, this works

Review: Whoever made this does not understand how stringed instruments work.  This is a cheap version of a lyre and would not work to be a playing instrument at all.  It looks nice, but will not stay in tune.  I have a well-made lyre that I can add the tuner, tune each string and it stays in tune - at least as with many instruments, for a time.  Stringed instruments, staying in tune can be affected by humidity, cold or really hot weather an how you play.  But if you can't get it tuned in the first place, then what good is it?

Title: ~1 year later, and still in search of a quality, durable stand Review: After a year of regular use, this stand is completely inoperable. The top part of the stand does not stay secured to the bottom (stripped screw). I appreciate the modular design to an extent, but more parts = more opportunity for failure. This stand was a huge disappointment after thinking I was making a solid investment.

I'm leaning towards buying cheaper stands and just replacing them 1-2 a year rather than dropping almost $90 bones on something that advertises quality.

Title: Ernie Ball Regular Slinky Nickel Wound Sets, .010 - .046 (3 Pack)

Review: I purchased these Ernie Ball Regular Slinky Nickel Wound Sets, .010 - .046 (3 Pack), offering to have around when my strings start to go bad.  They are comfortable enough and the quality seems good.  I do like them well enough to buy more in the future.  I'm not sure they are all that Slinky for what it is worth.

Title: Works fine, Visually Disappointing

Review: Tone is good, price is fair.  Wooden base build quality is terrible.  The metal chime is suspended on the wood base at four points with string, but the four cuts in the wood are all at different places and angles, as if this was done by four different people without even measuring the locations and cuts.  It would be easy to use a ruler to mark this and would have made the visual appeal so much better and not cost any more.  A shame to ruin a beautiful instrument with some shoddy assembly.  Takes away from the balance and harmony.

Title: Best Guitar Strings in the World

Review: Both my husband and I have electric guitars. One can never have enough guitar strings!  These are Slinky.  The Ball family have been making guitar strings since 1962. Not many USA companies can claim that long duration anymore with all the mergers and acquisitions of today. So you know the Ball family are the experts, right?! They've been around as long as I can remember and were on the cutting edge of rock and roll back in the day. Their Paradigm guitar strings for electric and acoustic are the worlds strongest and best technology you'll ever find. And they back their products with a full guarantee if the strings breaks or rust within 90 days they will replace it. But I don't believe you'd ever have to worry about that as these are super-durable and break resistant.

Title: Good product for a small lighting setup

Review: It's a nice product and is good if for smaller jobs if you do not want to use dmx. I do suggest that you get the wifi hub for it so you can use the phone / ipad app. It seems to be reliable and easy to set up. I've had no problems with it as of yet. And if you dont wanna use the wifi hub the remote works but the touch sensitive buttons can be annoying. It will pickup even the lightest touch so be aware of that. Overall its a good product and the only thing that I didn't care for was the sensitivity of the remote.

Title: Honer has an excellent reputation, but this harmonica did not meet the ...

Review: The harmonica had a shrill, tinny sound and seemed to be lacking in lower register notes. Honer has an excellent reputation, but this harmonica did not meet the standard I was expecting.  I have played Honer Harmonica for years and have not heard a sound this bad from any of them.

Title: Wonderfully crafted!!! Beautiful Sound!!! Review: [[VIDEOID:324fac2b754dbb4dd451e0e516211654]] This 23” concert Ukulele is made of beautiful Sapele wood. The grain on this one looks amazing too. Moreover, the craftsmanship is top notch. No jagged frets, low action, straight neck, the nut is perfectly set, and beautiful binding. The sound is really good and the notes are clear. Good beginners and beyond!!! I will be playing this in church mic’d up, because it sounds that good.

Trust you found this review honest and helpful:-)

Title: Nothing horrible about these picks, but I'm not a fan of the material.

Review: These picks look good, and while the hole in the center doesn't really seem to help me personally, others might really like it. My issue with them is that they are made of a very stiff/smooth plastic. I think it's delrin, but since I don't see that confirmed in the description, it's just my guess. The bee graphic (which is only on one side) is the only place that seems to grip for me. If you held your picks a little tighter than I do, so you could make more use of the hole in the middle, these might work really well. They just aren't for me. The delrin (assuming I'm right about that) is also much stiffer than a normal pick, so while these pics are .80 mil, they feel more like 1.00 or so. It's subtle, and probably not worth griping about, but they do feel different from typical picks.

Title: Bummed, I would pass on these if you like mid or low bass they are Neutral and treble only monitors

Review: im dumbfounded i read all the great reviews and purchased these, my daily drivers are  Senn. HD6XX, these more expensive cans pale in comparison?? i almost wonder if im doing something wrong, im using a mayflower arc and the low mid and vocals are amazing on the HD6XX They could use a tiny bit more treble, any way the t60s bass distorts on most songs with mid to low bass notes, the are incredibly neutral and high? completrey missing most parts of movie scores or reggae that i listen too?? im returning them bummed as i passed on Argons for these...

Title: Love Gudetama and the quirkiness of the Otamatone Review: The Otamatone is an interesting instrument, and I love that they have licensed gudetama to combine two things I love.

I probably wouldn't give one of these to a kid unless you really aren't bothered by random sounds (then again, it could be a great gift to kids of people I dislike I suppose).

Title: Some Nice Features But Uncomfortable

Review: These headphones seem well built. I like the features designed to specifically appeal to DJs, namely the detachable locking cord and the swivel mechanism. Both work well and are useful. Sound quality is okay; I was expecting something cleaner and brighter. But the deal breaker for me is that they are just uncomfortable. Both the headband and the cups are annoying. The band in particular is too tight and the phones press uncomfkrtably. The aforementioned pro features are attractive but I find these difficult to wear for an extended period of time.

Title: Three Stars

Review: Did not make me sound like EH.

Title: So much better than a “power strip”!

Review: Very nicely designed with built-in cord management and widely spaced outlets on one side and more tightly spaced on the other side. Way better than a ‘power strip’. I will say that mine had something knocking around inside of it. I opened it up and found a large loose blob of solder. I put the cover back on and all is well. I think it is a fluke and am sticking with my 5-star rating.

Title: Sustain, sustain!!

Review: There is not much to say about a tuning fork, except it is accurate and has great sustain. If it is accurate and rings long enough for me to get it to my ear to tune my instrument, I am satisfied. I have a tuning fork that does not ring long enough for me. I like to check my tuning several times to be sure my ears get it.

Title: Huge fan of KZ, just not these

Review: I've been using the KZ ZAS as my daily driver (Worship singer, acoustic guitar player), and I have been thrilled with them until the right side started having issues. Since these were a more recent release, I thought I would give them a try. That's what I get for not just being content with what I had, lol. I use a wireless IEM pack and I had to have the volume turned up all the way in order to be able to play and sing. By comparison, the zas only needed to be at 50% and was almost too loud.  The sound was not near as full as the zas. This is the first time that I've ever been disappointed in a set of KZ's. Hopefully, this will save someone else from making the same mistake.

Title: Worth trying out.  Among the best.

Review: Pricey and hard to acquire, but works as advertised.

Title: No way to teach kids unless you buy additional product like sticker or paint pens

Review: Ukulele works okay for a plastic version but I should have looked closer and noticed the frets are plastic and black on black fretboard. No way to see frets. No way to teach kids unless you buy additional product like sticker or paint pens.

Title: A little spotty but decent product

Review: I bought this little stereo to use at my apartment community events. It has pretty decent volume for how little it is, and the mic capability is awesome. My only complaint, which I was able to work around, was that the mic volume would unexpectedly drop sometimes and I would have to turn the speaker off and then back on the get back up to the volume I needed. I'm sure I may just have a wonky one. Other than that, the speaker was just what I needed.

Title: Screw sizes were a tiny bit off Review: These fit an Epiphone Special I with a very tight squeeze.
- there is a little bit of scratchy/scuff marks, but it wasnt worth returning.

Title: Have sent 2 back already - not worth it

Review: These speakers come either blown or will vibrate as if blown after first 15 minutes. Could have been a good product if the speaker was not so prone to defect. Am going to try the Aker 16w. This is NOT a 50w speaker. Open the box and the instructions say 12w.

Title: Poor packaging

Review: Cheap packaging ruined this experience for me. Instead of packaging each string separately, they wrapped them all together in one jumbled mass of wire inside a sealed plastic sleeve. The high E and B strings were severely kinked in several places, which made unwrapping all the strings very difficult  The E and B were unusable.The remaining strings are now spares.

Title: Beautiful guitar.. that won’t stay in tune.

Review: As with others reviews I have seen on this PRS Zach Myers, I too have had constant problems with the guitar staying in tune. I had it set up professionally twice. The truss rod/neck angle was adjusted, new strings installed. It just won’t stay in tune. Too bad because I love the look of the guitar. Too bad it has all these tuning issues. If you want a real PRS with less headaches you need to go up to their S2 or Custom line.

Title: Makes my $1000 condenser microphone sound worse than my laptop's built-in microphone

Review: If you need XLR to USB because you want to make higher quality recordings, this is no good. Low gain settings fail to adequately record timbre, and high gain settings introduce noise.

Title: Downgraded score: Adhesion is terrible!

Review: It's a real shame. I purchased these about 7 months ago and the adhesion stickers they came with have never once failed in that time. I just bought three more packs and the stickers are different, I can't even keep up with the panels falling off the wall. Whatever they switched ruined this product for me. Not returning them as it isn't worth the hassle, but I'm not thrilled to be going out to buy actual adhesive stickers which they should've provided in the first place.

Title: Good Strings

Review: They are decent average strings. Not bad by any means nothing to jump up and down for either. Mainly bought them for the Merlin I purchased as they were the only available string set I am aware of for this instrument. Seagull recommends them as well.

Title: Possible QC problems at CAD, test your unit. Overall, a nice microphone

Review: It's a nice mic, I think it's quality for voice is really very good. I like the form factor. I too, however, had a quality control problem. The grill was mounted about 5 degrees off, rotated just enough to make it distraction every time I looked at it. I kept asking myself: Why? It seemed so obvious, didn't someone notice before shipping it off? Finally, I sent it back to CAD and they replaced the grill at no charge, but still, they may have a QC problem at the factory, which apparently has affected the sonic performance of some units. Too bad, if this is happening to more than a few mics out of a few thousand, CAD needs to tighten things up. For what it's worth, one guy I communicated with via email was very helpful and got things done. Another guy I caught on the phone had a real attitude. I don't know, maybe it was a bad day, or maybe there's some dysfunction in the business. My view is that CAD needs to take their production and customer service up a notch, understanding that nobody actually has to buy their stuff; they choose to buy their stuff . . . and choices are abundant in the microphone industry.

Title: There's a screw in the middle of it that will ...

Review: There's a screw in the middle of it that will dig into your end pin. The foam on the bottom isn't grippy at all and cello slips away. I'm returning

Title: Hard Heads

Review: The hard rubber heads of these mallets might work well with your standard drums, but they were too hard and harsh for a steel tongue drum.  Cotton balls and duct tape fixed them.

Title: easy to use Review: The first one I got didn't work, but Amazon replaced it with one that does.
Pros: Just gives you a count, no emphasis on a particular beat; easy to use; doesn't use an app so no data is collected; sits up well because of the little bail on the back, sound plus light.
Cons: Not many, pretty handy little gadget; not a whole lot of features or versatility; a little expensive for what you get.

Title: Great Guitar for kids or the elderly

Review: Great little guitar set for a kid !! I use it with senior citizens in the nursing home and will probably buy two more for other folks.  It sounds decent and feels sturdy.  This is not a concert instrument and nice way to start or just to have a guitar to play with for a child, disabled adult or the elderly!!

Title: Great sound but fragile.

Review: I love the plucky sounds. The red series allows you to use these gut-like strings in standard slots. However they are somewhat fragile.

Title: Terrible volume!!

Review: Tried to put the volume to the max capacity, and it was still very quiet. This would only work if you hook it up to a louder speaker and crank up the volume. Still in search of a better alternative..

Title: It fits!

Review: I bought this as a gift for my son's golf clubs so he could take them with him after a Christmas visit.  His standard golf bag fit fine but his driver had to be packed next to the bag, not in it.  It made it back to his home with no problems and seemed to protect the clubs well.  I think the price we paid was RELATIVELY good, but these things are expensive for what they are-a big hunk of plastic.  I guess they figure if you can afford to travel by air and take golf clubs with you, you probably have some money...

Title: You get what you pay for

Review: Customer service for this product was fantastic. Unfortunately the original one we bought, and the replacement one the company sent us, were both unable to be tuned. So, if you really aren't interested in quality sound, but want something to play with, I'd recommend this instrument, but not for serious learning.

Title: spend more money

Review: I'm disabled musician and suffer from dizziness and  vertigo I wanted a stool for playing guitar and piano but this throne feels wobbly and unstable

Title: Good idea, but not needed for front porch picking.

Review: I gave these a good trial and in the end I think they're too clunky for traditional music with an open backed wooden banjo. They give a tinny sound which is the way commercial bluegrass sounds, but in the end I've gone back to bare fingernails. Some of the banjo and guitar finger pickers around here will get a manicure on their playing hand and clear polish the nails but that sounds like too much artificiality to me.

Title: The plastic is great for his allergy but the chin rest is not ...

Review: Got this because my son is allergic to the metal on his original viola chin rest.  The plastic is great for his allergy but the chin rest is not as comfortable as the wooden one he had.  Cant have everything.

Title: fun guitar. Very good for beginners Review: The guitar stayed in tune through many playing sessions so far while only needing slight adjustments. It plays very well, and I would recommend it to a beginner guitarist

The skull design on it is a nice added touch to my skull lover.

Title: Garbage quality

Review: Two of the four strings unwound immediately. Garbage quality.

Title: Gorgeous Quality and Terrible Sound

Review: I got this for my Fender American Special Stratocaster, I wanted to make it look a bit more elegant.  And it did.  But unfortunately it killed the tone of the guitar.  Because it's a big chunk of aluminum, it killed all the high frequencies, making the Strat not sound like a Strat anymore.  I guess if you've got a horribly bright guitar this would work great, but on a typical guitar it just kills the highs and makes it sound bad.  That all being said, it does look good and the quality was top-notch.  Plus all the screw holes lined up.

Title: Average Quality, Two Stones Stuffed into Tight Packaging Review: This is a combination green jade roller with two gua sha stones set. The jade roller is of average quality - not great but not bad - somewhere in-between. The main thing is that the packaging was very frugal, a simple narrow box with a roller and two gua sha stones stuffed into it. Fortunately the stones were securely wrapped up in bubble wrap; however they are on the small side and noticeably thinner than other stand-alone Gua Sha stones I've ordered in the past.

Title: MY GUITAR AMP SOUNDED MUCH BETTER Review: I wanted a home karaoke setup, and others have said it's best to not use your home theater for the vocals since it can damage the speakers.

So I bought two wireless microphones and hooked them up to this (I bought the 8" speaker), and played the music through my home theater system. It sounded great at a low volume, but who wants to sing karaoke at a low volume? At a high volume (45 dB setting on my Denon for the music, 80-90% max volume for this speaker), the sound quality was really bad. At 100% max volume for this speaker, the quality was even worse, and there was a ton of feedback.

I plugged the microphones into the "INSERT" slot on my 20 year-old guitar amp (I have a CRATE - GFX65T, which has a 12" speaker. It is absolutely nothing special, I think I paid $150 for it 20 years ago) using the CLEAN setting and the max volume was about the same as this speaker. But the sound quality was so much better!

If you are using this for vocals only, then I highly recommend finding a new/used guitar amp online with a "clean" setting instead of this speaker. You can get used guitar amps for the same price as this and I think you'll be happier. Plus, you might be able to go into a guitar store, bring your microphones, and just try out some of the amps there before committing to buying anything. I think the amp I bought now retails for $325 which is crazy to me so maybe you'll need to spend that much money to get a good speaker, I don't know. Good luck!

Title: The perfect low cost stand Review: I have experienced no problems with this stand for either live or home studio use. In fact, I had been using [[ASIN:B000978D58 On Stage Stands MS7701 Tripod Boom Microphone Stand]] which are not as well made based on problems I have had. To be fair, the On Stage stand is excellent for light gigging and home studio use, but not nearly as sturdy or as versatile as this stand.

The best feature is the fact that you can place a voice mic at the top of the stand, which has a normal threaded post, and also use the boom for another microphone. Or leave off the top mic and just use the boom. Where this comes in handy is the stand will allow someone who plays both flute and saxophone, for example, to pre-set the mic placements and use a single stand for both. Or, for crowded stages, two vocalists can share the same stand, or instrumentalists (or a combination.)

Another use is to add another boom to the top post for overhead mic placement. One boom I use (and recommend) is the [[ASIN:B0002T67K6 On Stage MSA7040TB Adjustable Microphone Boom, Black]].

Overall, this is a nicely built, versatile stand that will withstand moderate gigging (not sturdy enough for touring), and a great addition to any home studio.

Title: Excellent Introduction Review: this is an easy to follow beginner's guide to the harp. The progression is logical and each chapter builds upon the previous one. It includes everything from how to sit and finger placement to octave jumps, reading music and of course some tunes to execute. The ink illustrations are clear. There are also some photos that are not that great but they just illustrate the different types of heart. There is a glossary and an additional ten scores in the back.

I play the piano, pipe organ and mandolin. I have been considering investing in a harp and this book provided a solid introduction to the instrument and the technique. The book is understandable but not necessarily easy. the lessons do have to be studied and practiced to realize the benefit. But overall it is an excellent and thorough introduction to a beautiful instrument.

Title: Easy to Use and Smoother Skin Results Review: Wearing flip-flops or sandals always gives me unsightly heel calluses. Using a pumice stone just isn’t as effective as a foot file. I felt no discomfort at all. Then to achieve an even smoother skin, I used the foot rasp afterwards. Just by using the rasp 10 seconds back and forth over the tough areas really does the job.

I am really amazed at how well it works. My heels never felt so smooth. It actually feels almost therapeutic knowing that my feet is well-groomed. The rasp has 2 sides, but I don’t see much difference between the two. Both sides work just as well. I recommend cleaning the file and rasp with soap and water, and then final cleaning with rubbing alcohol to prevent infection. My package also came with 5 tiny dehydrated towels. The results of my heels are great! I would definitely recommend this product.

Not what I expected for something labeled as a "hard case."

My Seagull dreadnought fits a bit loosely and slides up and down. My Martin dreadnought fits better. The case is fairly deep, which means a bit more room in the goody box under the neck. But it's also bulkier and a bit more awkward to carry than my previous case. This case feels heavy, even when empty. The leather handle actually has sharp seams and isn't particularly comfortable. And the case didn't come with the pick sampler, which isn't a big deal except that a product should come with what it says it should come with.

I don't dislike this enough to return it. It looks nice and it's okay for toting my guitar locally. But I wouldn't buy it again.

Title: Zippers tend to break, but otherwise sturdy Review: I play minimal kits, usually a bass drum, rack and floor toms, snare drum, hi-hats and one or two ride cymbals. This bag easily holds my hardware, which is the [[ASIN:B0002F4ZSQ Drum Workshop CP6500 6000 Series Hi-Hat Stand-Flush Base]], [[ASIN:B001U0ORMG DW Drum Workshop SM770 Bass Drum Mounted Cymbal Arm w/L-Arm & Bracket]], [[ASIN:B0014DK7E6 Drum Workshop CP6710 6000 Series Straight Cymbal Stand Flush Base]], [[ASIN:B000VTDLT2 Gibraltar 8606 Flat Base Snare Stand]] and whichever bass drum pedal and throne I happen to be using on a given night.

What drives me crazy about this bag is that it's the perfect size, the wheels are convenient and the handles and straps are heavy duty ... but the zippers on two of the three I have owned have broken. What I mean by that is the shuttle part of the zipper on both have come completely out of the tracks, and on one the pull tab broke off.

Fortunately, the top flap on the bag has a velcro catch that allows me to close it. This does not help, though, if I am moving it from my car to a venue in the rain, my hardware will get wet, which was not the case when the zippers worked,

Despite my complaints, this particular bag model is perfect for my needs in all other respects and I will probably continue buying them to replace the ones I have when they finally wear out.

Title: Budget price, but built to last Review: This is a budget-priced stand that actually exceeds my needs. The top shaft can be reversed from 1 3/8 inches to 1.5 inches, and it has a locking pen for safety and convenience.

Since I needed a lighter pole this one is priced perfectly for my budget. If you are using monster speakers this stand is obviously a bad choice, but for 15 inch unpowered mains down to the smaller speakers that I use this is a bargain. It's well built and mine have withstood many gigs with a lot of life left in them.
