Title: Only use in an emergency Review: These strips are relatively thick and stiff and are not truly optimum for attaching snare wire sets to your throw-off and butt.

A better solution is grosgrain ribbon, such as [[ASIN:B007K0TK04 Grosgrain Ribbon 5/8 Inch 30 Yards White]] (or a color of your choice). In most cases the simple (and inexpensive) replacement of the plastic snare wire straps with grosgrain ribbon will result in an immediately noticeable improvement in snare response. Do a search and you will get a large number of hits confirming this.

Most plastic snare straps are 3/8" wide, but I typically buy 5/8" wide grosgrain ribbon because it perfectly fits every snare drum throwoff and butt I've used it with. The thinner, 3/8" ribbon can cock when threading it through the strainer and butt clamps, skewing your wires. I've uploaded a customer-supplied image of one of my snare drums outfitted with grosgrain ribbon to show what I am talking about.

This plastic model is OK in an emergency, but should not be a long term fix if you must install it.

You are simply directed to some third-party website where you can download a crippled, time-limited trial of some software that they want you to buy. Totally classless.

Since all of the "good" features are in the software (they you don't actually get) you aren't really getting much here. Definitely not enough to justify the price. Title: Could use better strings

Review: As you'd imagine this is like a 2 year Olds size if this were a guitar, but it's not a guitar, just used that for a visual/mental reference for anyone trying to picture its size. It is a decent little beginner instrument, but I do have issues with the string. Even if you adjust it it just doesn't quite have the right sound, and it feels more like a toy than an actual instrument to practice on. It came with a carry bag which is a bonus, but the Box is shaped that you could store it in there as well. But by far the only flaw I've encountered is the strings. I can't get past the fact that I feel they need to be switched out with something a better quality. Still, if you're trying to get your little ones into music, this would be a great start. It's not loud and obnoxious, like some instruments can be. And the price is fair enough, that you could purchase this, and if your little one didn't really fall into the music loving part, it wouldn't be a waste. It would definitely be great to give to a child to test whether or not musics something they want to pursue.

Title: Basic stand

Review: It requires assembly. Not at all rocket science, but seems like it would have only taken them springing for a slightly larger box, with the weight unaffected. Assembly in under 10 minutes, just attaching the feet to the top and bottom. Requires included allen wrench. The feet are different sizes, and not labelled, so just pay attention to the top/bottom (the larger ones go on the bottom). Also, for a minute, I thought mine had been shipped without the required hex bolts, but they were screwed into the legs. Which was a relief, but also annoying, because unscrewing them, only to reattach with the foot effectively doubled the assembly time.  I wish it was taller. Can only be used seated. I like to stand and play from time to time.

Title: Nice, But Could Be Improved Review: I bought this for my husband since he loves singing while he's playing the guitar or keyboard. I attached the microphone which fit just fine into the end of it. It's easy to set up and it reaches a really nice height. He likes that he can sing into the microphone, hands-free.
The price was also not too expensive. I looked at similar ones and bought this one since it looked nice online and was one of the cheapest.
The reason I did not give this product five stars is because after a while the microphone part will drop down from the weight. It is really not very heavy so this kind of frustrates me. My husband and I have to keep picking it back up. If this were improved, then, the product would be perfect.
